question: A wholesaler buys a batch of ceiling fans at a 50% markup over the factory's base cost ₹C. He then allows a 20% trade discount to the retailer. The retailer applies a 40% markup on his cost and offers a flat 10% discount to customers on the printed price. If a customer finally pays ₹18,144, what is the original base cost (₹C) of one ceiling fan from the factory?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Applying successive percentage multipliers on the base cost C yields the final selling price:

Final SP = C × 1.5 (markup) × 0.8 (discount) × 1.4 (markup) × 0.9 (discount)

⇒ 18144 = C × 1.2 × 1.26

⇒ 18144 = 1.512C

⇒ C = 18144 ÷ 1.512 = 12000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Factory base cost = ₹ C

Wholesaler markup = 50%, Trade discount = 20%

Retailer markup = 40%, Customer discount = 10%

Final amount paid by customer = ₹18,144

**Calculations:**

⇒ Wholesaler Marked Price (MP) = C × (1 + 50 ÷ 100) = 1.5C

⇒ Retailer Cost Price (CP) = 1.5C × (1 − 20 ÷ 100) = 1.5C × 0.8 = 1.2C

⇒ Retailer Marked Price (MP) = 1.2C × (1 + 40 ÷ 100) = 1.2C × 1.4 = 1.68C

⇒ Final Selling Price (SP) = 1.68C × (1 − 10 ÷ 100) = 1.68C × 0.9 = 1.512C

Equating this to the final amount paid:

⇒ 1.512C = 18144

⇒ C = 18144 ÷ 1.512

⇒ C = 12000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes multiple sequential percentage changes (like markup followed by discount), the final value is found by multiplying the initial base value by the combined multiplying factors (1 + R ÷ 100) or (1 − R ÷ 100).

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (also known as Printed Price or Label Price) and never on the Cost Price. Formula: Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 − Discount%).

Effective Discount Formula

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount percentage is given by the formula: (a + b − a × b ÷ 100)%.
